subject: Technical deep dive — latency/throughput SLOs and deployment topology
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@acme.com>
Cc: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-30T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Technical deep dive — latency/throughput SLOs and deployment topology

Hi Tom / Elena,

Thanks again for taking the time today — good to meet the Acme team. Quick recap from our call and the follow-ups we agreed on. Please reply with any corrections.

Customer pain points and goals (as discussed):
- Current inference latency spikes and high tail latency (p95) impacting user experience for the realtime summarization feature.
- Throughput variability during peak traffic leads to degraded batch jobs and cost surprises.
- Strong security/compliance requirements: VPC peering, SOC 2 evidence, and customer-managed KMS for keys.

SLOs you called out (please confirm):
- Latency: p95 <= 150 ms for single-turn text generation (avg payload ~256 tokens).
- Throughput: steady-state 250 req/s with bursts to 1,500 req/s for short windows.
- Availability: 99.95% regionally (us-west).

Model & topology notes from the call:
- Preferred model family: mix of 13B-class models for generation and smaller 2-4B models for embedding/reranking.
- Preference for private/dedicated capacity due to data residency and predictable cost.

Next steps (owners & ETA):
1) Redwood: send a proposed deployment topology (dedicated vs private options), sizing estimate, and preliminary cost delta — target EOD tomorrow. (Owner: Marissa)
2) Redwood: provide a short technical note on quantization and expected p95 improvements with int8/int4 paths. (Owner: Dev)
3) Acme: confirm the payload size distribution and any additional security controls required (e.g., specific KMS/HSM vendor). (Owner: Tom/Elena)
4) Schedule a follow-up 30-45min call next week to review sizing and hit the numbers.

Attachments: acme-slo-requirements.xlsx (you shared this in the call), redwood-deployment-diagram.png

Thanks — I’ll loop in engineering to follow up on the sizing.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Marissa — thanks for the recap and for the fast follow. All looks good; a couple clarifications: 

- The p95 target is for the user-facing endpoint (single-turn generation) only — background batch jobs can tolerate higher latency.
- Payload distribution: ~70% of calls are short (<=128 tokens), ~25% mid (129-512), ~5% long (>512) — we’ll attach a sample distribution after this email.
- Security: we need VPC peering and customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS) for key wrapping. SOC 2 evidence is required for procurement.

We’re interested in a reserved dedicated pool (monthly commit) if the numbers make sense vs a private VPC deployment.

I’ll upload the sample payload CSV to the shared drive and confirm availability for next Wed (May 5) 10:00am PT.

Thanks,
Tom
Director of Product, Acme Corp

Subject: Re: Technical deep dive — latency/throughput SLOs and deployment topology (sizing & topology notes)

Folks — following up with the technical notes we discussed on the call. High-level recommendations and assumptions below. I attached a quick sizing CSV with cost/throughput tradeoffs.

Assumptions:
- Typical request is generation with ~256 tokens output; 70% of requests are short (<=128 tokens) as Tom noted.
- Target endpoint p95 <= 150 ms.
- Workload is bursty: baseline 250 req/s, 1-2 minute bursts to 1,500 req/s.

Options (summary):
1) Hosted — Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pool)
   - Single-region dedicated pool (us-west) with autoscaled buffer capacity for short bursts.
   - Recommended hardware: H100 (preferred) or A100 depending on availability; H100 gives ~20-30% lower p95 for 13B-class models when using int8 kernels.
   - Expected perf: With optimized kernels + int8 quantization and dynamic batching, we estimate p95 ~110-140 ms for 256-token gen on H100 (13B) at steady-state.

2) Private (VPC / on-prem)
   - Same runtime but deployed in your VPC with private control plane. Slightly higher setup time and capex/contract overhead.
   - Good for maximum data control and compliance (customer-managed KMS).

Sizing notes:
- For steady 250 req/s (mix of short/mid), a small cluster of 2x H100 instances with batching and prefix caching should be sufficient; to handle 1,500 req/s bursts we recommend either:
   a) pre-warmed burst capacity (reserved extra GPUs) or
   b) short-term autoscale on Dedicated with burst credits (preferred for cost predictability).

- Memory/KV cache: if you expect long-context sessions with KV reuse, we need to size for KV cache per-shard. Let us know expected concurrent sessions and average context length.

Security/compliance:
- VPC peering supported for Private deployments; SOC 2 evidence package and KMS integration docs attached.

Attachments: sizing-estimate.csv (simple cost/throughput table)

Next technical steps:
- I’ll prepare a concrete topology diagram with exact GPU counts and a cost delta between Dedicated vs Private by EOD tomorrow.
- If you can share sample payload distribution and concurrency numbers, I’ll include them in the sizing.

—Dev
Dev Patel
Principal Infrastructure SWE | Redwood Inference
dev.patel@redwood.com
